drafted_from: tools/social-posts/tool-rows.json (tool:send-each-post-at-its-time), read-data/send-a-post.mjs (sendEachPostAtItsTime), read-data/posts.json (at_its_time), test/send-a-post.test.mjs; the example was run on the test fixture
start_here: Say to your AI: "Switch on the wake that sends each post at its time, so a post I set to go at 2026-01-02 midnight UTC is sent then to every account it names." It runs when your posts change; it sends nothing itself and sets one timed send for each destination.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads the post and connection records the wake was granted and answers the timed sends to set, writing no record itself.
instructions: 1. Draft a post and approve it (tool:draft-a-post, tool:approve-a-post), and connect each account it goes to.
2. Say "Set that post to go at its time": the AI runs tool:set-a-post-to-go-at-its-time, which arms the post (armed_at) for its scheduled_for time.

3. Switch on the wake of tool:send-each-post-at-its-time once (its wake name is at-its-time). From then on each time your posts change it runs with the changed record ids and sets one timed run of the place's send row (tool:send-a-post-to-<place>) per destination still to be sent, at scheduled_for. Nothing is polled.

4. Read what it answers: set (each post, account, send tool and time), left_out (each send not set and why: the account is no longer connected, or more than 32 sends in one firing) and said. A post taken back, changed or set again sends nothing at the old time, because each timed send checks the post still carries the armed_at it was set with.

worked_examples.title: One armed post for one X account sets one timed send
worked_examples.ask: Send my approved post at its time to my second X account.
worked_examples.given: From tools/social-posts/test/send-a-post.test.mjs (the first send-each-post-at-its-time test, run here on its fixture): the wake fires with the change of post:p1, a scheduled post with caption "A short post", destinations [service_connection:x:second], approved, armed_at 2026-01-01T00:00:05.000Z and scheduled_for 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z; that X connection is on file. The run is woken by the engine with the changed record ids, so the input is empty.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"set":[{"post_id":"post:p1","account_id":"service_connection:x:second","tool":"tool:send-a-post-to-x","at":"2026-01-02T00:00:00Z"}],"left_out":[],"said":"1 sends are set to go at their time."}; the engine is also handed one timed run of tool:send-a-post-to-x at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z with input {post_id: "post:p1", account_id: "service_connection:x:second", armed_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:05.000Z"}. The wake writes nothing; a draft, a post already posted to that account or a removed post answers no send and said "No changed post is set to go at its time, so nothing was set."
